core_obligations: Reduce to the case Y = Spec(B) for a ring B using the local criterion for quasi-compactness (proof lines 1693-1700).
Write X as the union of quasi-compact open subspaces X_i obtained from an affine open covering of a surjective etale U -> X, and record that X_i -> Y is quasi-compact (proof lines 1703-1708).

Form T = Spec(B[a_i ; i in I]), T_i = D(a_i) and the reduced closed subspace Z of T x_Y X with |Z| = |T x_Y X| minus the union of the |T_i x_Y X_i|, with its base change diagram (proof lines 1709-1726).

Prove the claim that some point y of Y has no affine open neighbourhood V with X_V quasi-compact, and fix the point t of T over y with kappa(t) = kappa(y) and a_i = 1 in kappa(t) (proof lines 1730-1744).

Assume f_T(|Z|) is closed, extract g in B[a_i ; i in I] with f_T(|Z|) contained in V(g) and t not in V(g), and choose a point x of |X_V| outside the X_j for the finite set J of variables appearing in g (proof lines 1747-1755).
Construct t' in T over v with t' not in V(g) and t' in V(a_i) for i not in J, lift it to a point of |Z|, and contradict f_T(|Z|) contained in V(g) (proof lines 1756-1770).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma stating that a universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S is quasi-compact (source lines 1684-1688). The argument is a full constructive proof, not a citation: after the reduction to Y = Spec(B) through the local criterion for quasi-compactness, it covers X by quasi-compact open subspaces X_i obtained from an affine open covering of a surjective etale U -> X, builds the reduced closed subspace Z of T x_Y X with |Z| = |T x_Y X| minus the union of the |T_i x_Y X_i| for T = Spec(B[a_i]) and T_i = D(a_i), and then shows f_T(|Z|) is not closed. The non-routine step is the choice of the point y over which no affine neighbourhood V has X_V quasi-compact, together with the finite set J of variables occurring in a hypothetical g vanishing on f_T(|Z|): from these it produces a point x in |X_V| outside the X_j for j in J and a point t' of T over v with t' not in V(g) and t' in V(a_i) for i not in J, contradicts f_T(|Z|) contained in V(g).
